title: Export is not implemented
body:
Every report subcommand (`analyze`, `filter-users`, `engagement`, `growth trend`, `growth bulk-invite`) accepts `--export <path>` and writes the report as `.csv` when the path ends in `.csv` and as `.xlsx` when it ends in `.xlsx`; any other extension raises `ValueError`. Column headers are snake_case and stable across runs. CSV and XLSX exports emit columns in the insertion order of the keys of the first input row (after header normalization), and this order is preserved across runs. `tg_automation.export.export_report(rows, path)` accepts dicts or any object exposing `as_dict()`; its header-normalization helper `_normalize_field(name)` lowercases, trims surrounding whitespace, and replaces non-alphanumeric runs with single underscores (so `"Messages Sent"` and `"Reactions-Given"` become `messages_sent` and `reactions_given`).

The repository includes `docs/output_schema.md`, documenting the output schema for analysis, engagement, growth, and export rows. The document must enumerate every exported field using snake_case names. `docs/output_schema.md` documents every field in markdown tables whose first column is the field name wrapped in backticks, for example a row like `| user_id | int | ... |` should be written with `user_id` backticked in the first column, so each documented field name is parseable as the first backticked token of a table row. Non-field type names or implementation identifiers should not be backticked unless they are listed in a field-name column.

`solve.sh` installs all runtime and test dependencies (including `openpyxl` for XLSX export) so that `pytest -q /tests/` passes when invoked after `solve.sh`.
acceptance_hint: 6 executable checks over the export surface.
